Surah "Al-Qari'ah" (The Striking)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Al-Qari'ah﴾ is the subject (mubtada').

"What" is the second subject (mubtada' thani), and "the Striking Calamity" (al-qari'ah) is its predicate (khabar). The clause (al-jumlah) is the predicate of the first subject. The original form would have been "what is it," but He repeated the noun to magnify its importance.
﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ That is: what thing made you know what it is? And from where did you come to know that?

﴿Yawma﴾ (on the Day) is in the accusative, governed by an implied verb indicated by "al-Qari'ah" (the Striking Calamity), or the implied meaning is: it strikes on the Day ﴿when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾. He likened them to moths in their multitude, their dispersion, their weakness, their lowliness, and their scattering toward the caller from every side, just as moths fly toward the fire. It is called "farash" (moth) because of its spreading out (tafarrush) and its dispersal (intishar).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 101, verse 5:

﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up.﴾ He likened the mountains to *al-ʿihn* (العِهْنِ), which is wool (*al-ṣūf*, الصُوفُ) dyed in various colours, because the mountains are of various colours,

﴿And among the mountains are streaks, white and red, of varying colours.﴾ [Fāṭir: 27], and to *al-manfūsh* (المَنفُوشِ) of it, because its parts are scattered.

(p-674) ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾, through their following the truth. The word "mawazin" (scales) is the plural of "mawzun" (that which has weight), which is the deed that has weight and worth in the sight of God; or it is the plural of "mizan" (scale), and its heaviness is its tipping (weighing down the pan).
﴿So he will be in a pleasing life﴾, one with contentment, or: one that is pleased with (i.e., approved of).
﴿And as for he whose scales are light﴾ — through his following falsehood.

﴿So his mother will be an abyss﴾, meaning his dwelling and refuge is the Fire. It is said that the word "umm" (mother) is applied to a refuge (ma'wa) by way of metaphor, because a mother is the shelter and refuge of her child.

10. ﴿And what will make you know what it is?﴾ The pronoun refers to "Hawiyah" (the Abyss), and the hā' is the hā' of pausal silence (hā' al-sakt, the hā' added for pause). Then he explained it, saying:
Fire blazing fiercely (نارٌ حامِيَةٌ): it has reached the utmost limit in heat.
